propositions: A rejected tickets-branch auto-push succeeds locally and reports only retry count, silently discarding the git rejection reason from stderr, leaving the divergence invisible to the writing agent.
Ticket comments are never scanned for secrets on write; the gitleaks code-review gate sees only code, not the raw environment output routinely pasted in comments.

The PUSH_PENDING divergence signal is pull-only (computed only in fsck.py), reachable solely from an explicit 'rebar fsck', so subsequent writes re-announce an identical one-shot warning rather than an escalating unpushed-commit backlog, explaining eight hours of undetected divergence.

The rejection-classification regex _NON_FF matches the substring 'rejected' in policy-decline lines like 'pre-receive hook declined', causing terminal rejections to be misrouted onto the retry path and skip the only stderr-bearing log call.

On sync.push=async, the push runs as a detached subprocess with stderr=DEVNULL, making warnings undeliverable to the writing agent, and library embedders receive only a NullHandler, also silencing the warning.
